clue.text: Spoiled American spat out overegged trifle?

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and messed about, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A grumpy American spits out a dessert that has far too much egg in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' looks like the pudding, but here it means a trivial matter, and overegging it means making far too much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a big fuss made over something minor, which is a trivial matter blown out of proportion.

clue.text: Roasts meat overnight, ultimately to go into buns

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word just before it, so only its final letter is kept
going into something means being placed inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: lamb is a kind of meat
buns is slang for the buttocks, as is ass
the final letter of overnight

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: roast meat slowly overnight, then serve it in bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roasts' looks like oven work but is the definition in its sense of harsh criticism; buns here are buttocks, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise them severely, which is exactly what attacking them verbally in this way means.

clue.text: Notorious fiddler has turned over capital for nothing

indicators.note: a capital letter turned on its side becomes a different letter, so one letter of the name is swapped for its rotated form

blocks.note: the Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A notorious violin player has flipped a capital city on its head for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is the capital letter N at the start of NERO: rotate it a quarter turn and it becomes Z, giving ZERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number that stands for none at all, a plain synonym of nothing.

clue.text: Complex booby traps are working

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it in, so the two pieces before it close round the next word

blocks.note: complex means difficult
a booby is a fool, as is a tit in British slang; both are also birds
A is the symbol for an are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Elaborate booby traps are in operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The container here is unusual: two pieces side by side close round the third rather than one word enclosing another. Tit is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard at it means being busy and labouring diligently on some task.

clue.text: Peaceful place outside of Earth

indicators.note: being outside something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a haven is a safe, quiet refuge
E is the standard abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Somewhere tranquil beyond our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes paradise: a place of bliss and rest believed to lie beyond the world.

clue.text: Low suppressed by this fizzy energy drink

indicators.note: fizzy suggests bubbling agitation, so the word beside it is stirred into a new order
something suppressed is held down inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
to low is to make the sound a cow makes
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down is perked up by a fizzy energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like a mood but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a thick blended beverage of fruit, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: You in Strasbourg? No, in Stuttgart - listen!

blocks.note: tu is French for you, and Strasbourg is in France
nein is German for no, and Stuttgart is in Germany

explanation.surface: Someone crossing the French-German border asks a question and gets a sharp answer, then demands attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune in is to set a radio to a station and pay attention to the broadcast.

clue.text: Lady turned green by fart, use toilet desperately

indicators.note: doing something desperately means doing it in a frantic, disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A woman goes green after a fart and dashes to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The New York monument was a copper colour when built and weathered to green.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous New York monument is a copper female figure whose surface oxidised to a green patina over time.

clue.text: Boring to have sex when the other person has no moves

definitions.text: when the other person has no moves

blocks.note: stale means dull and uninteresting
animals mate when they have sex

explanation.surface: A complaint that sex gets dull when the partner just lies there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No moves' sounds like the bedroom, but the definition is from chess.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is a drawn position where the player to move is not in check yet has no legal play.

clue.text: Ben Affleck's biggest character lacking in measure

indicators.note: lacking means going without something, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: an amount is a quantity or measure
the capital letter that starts Affleck, its largest character

explanation.surface: A film question: who is the main role Ben Affleck has played?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben Affleck' reads as one name, but 'Ben' is the definition: Scottish for a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A ben is a Scottish mountain peak, and a mount is another word for a mountain or hill.

clue.text: Red Cross stops outcome of exsanguination?

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece is placed inside the other like a stopper

blocks.note: draining someone of blood leaves O, nothing, followed by blood: no blood at all
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: The Red Cross intervenes to stop someone bleeding to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' looks like the charity, but Red is the definition and Cross gives just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxblood is a deep brownish shade of crimson, named for the colour of cattle blood.

clue.text: 5/10 - Fast & Furious

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
the digits of ten written as the letters I and O
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A film critic gives the movie Fast & Furious a middling five out of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the film title; the score splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent and furious both describe something done with great force and fierce, uncontrolled rage.

clue.text: Naval post held by Emma Stone

indicators.note: something held by the words that follow sits inside them, spread across the actress's name

blocks.note: found running across the two words of the name

explanation.surface: The actress Emma Stone has been given a job in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is the tall upright pole on a ship that carries the sails, a post on a vessel.

clue.text: Plain ring gets adjusted to fit a woman getting married?

indicators.note: something adjusted is altered and rearranged, so the letters are reordered
made to fit means made to accommodate something, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one
the bride-to-be is the hen at a hen party, the British name for a bachelorette party

explanation.surface: A wedding ring is resized to fit the bride's finger.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plain is Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, home of the ancient stone circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric monument is a circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, so it is literally a ring on a plain.

clue.text: "Elementary, Doctor Watson" - Sherlock's last point

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the name that follows is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E, east, is a compass point, here tacked on at the end

explanation.surface: Holmes's famous catchphrase to his sidekick, given as his final word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' starts the quotation but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal idiom for something easy, which is what elementary means here.

clue.text: Former copper cocked up, detective's cover is blown

indicators.note: a cover is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
cocked up means tilted upward, and in a down clue that sends letters reading bottom to top

blocks.note: ex means former
Plod is British slang for a police officer, from Mr Plod in Noddy
the first and last letters of detective

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman blunders and an undercover detective's identity is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover is blown' looks like a spy phrase, but blown alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exploded has been blown apart, as a bomb or tyre is blown up.

clue.text: Potentially drives TT circuit very strongly

blocks.note: two letters T, written out as words
a circuit is a ring, the shape of the letter O
ff is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist rides the Isle of Man TT course at full throttle.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race; 'drives' sounds like motoring but means golf shots.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeing off is starting a golf hole, often with a long shot from the tee, so it may involve hitting a drive.

clue.text: Etna billowing big smoke and grit

indicators.note: billowing smoke churns and swirls, so the volcano's name is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the Big Smoke is a nickname for London, a city

explanation.surface: Mount Etna erupts, sending out a plume of smoke and volcanic grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like volcanic debris but means determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means courage and persistence, the quality of holding on resolutely without giving up.

clue.text: Passing judgement you are essentially a bit weird

indicators.note: weird means strange and out of order, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: you're is in effect the sound of your, a common text-speak spelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a judgemental person they are being rather strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like a casual verb but refers to death.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper write-up after a death assesses the life of someone who has passed on, a verdict on their life.

clue.text: Walk over and queue where the bouncers are?

blocks.note: to tramp is to walk heavily
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
a line is a queue

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting into a nightclub: walk across and wait in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouncers are doormen in the surface but jumpers in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is the springy frame on which people jump up and down, so it is where things bounce.

clue.text: Dimension warping space-time

indicators.note: warping bends something out of shape, so the letters that follow are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sci-fi idea of a new dimension created by bending space-time.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is one facet or feature of a situation, which a dimension can also mean.

clue.text: Hide air-bed that's been delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered by speaking it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a Lilo is a British brand of inflatable mattress

explanation.surface: Someone hides inside the packaging of an inflatable mattress that has just arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' looks like a parcel arriving but means spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to keep out of sight and avoid attention, which is to stay hidden.

clue.text: Setter's going round holding in wee

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the letters are read from the other end
holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm
taken as written

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter, needing the toilet, keeps it in while going round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like urine but is the Scottish word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini means small in size, as does wee in Scottish usage.

clue.text: Dad about to take gentle wander back

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word before it is read the other way

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
p is piano, the musical mark for soft
to rove is to roam

explanation.surface: Father is about to go for a gentle stroll home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like the direction of the walk but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal is to support or endorse it, giving official agreement.

clue.text: Take remedy to keep fit

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a cure is a remedy
apt means suitable or fit

explanation.surface: Advice to take some medicine to stay healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like healthy but means suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To capture a prisoner or town is to seize it, one sense of take.

clue.text: Nose broken by the end of the game

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
a word broken by something is split open with it inserted in the gap

blocks.note: to nose about is to pry
the final letter of the

explanation.surface: A player's nose is broken at the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of the game' reads as one phrase, but game alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means animals hunted for sport or food, the same as quarry being chased.

clue.text: Cryptic clue cracked by new family member

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscured, so the word after it is scrambled
something cracked by another is broken open with it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A tricky crossword clue is solved by a newcomer to the family.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a parent's brother, a relative within a household or kin group.

clue.text: Running about then abrupt diarrhoea

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the last letter is chopped off

blocks.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
the trots is British slang for diarrhoea

explanation.surface: Someone dashes about after a sudden bout of diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' suggests the dash to the loo, but it means in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot is British idiom for in a row, consecutively, one after another without a break.
